Hi Marissa / Sarah —

Thanks for the details and the volume guidance. A few clarifications on AWS Marketplace private offers:

- Private offers allow the seller (Redwood) to propose custom pricing/terms for a specific buyer account; the PO can be structured as a unit-based SKU (e.g., per 1M tokens) or as a recurring subscription with usage tiers.
- Marketplace fees: AWS charges a marketplace fee on the seller side that varies by program (typically 3–15% depending on arrangements). That fee is usually taken from the seller payout — it doesn’t automatically get added to the buyer-facing price unless you choose to include it in the SKU price. In other words, if BrightCart wants to see $15 / 1M tokens on their invoice, Redwood would list $15 / 1M on the private-offer SKU and absorb/pay the marketplace fee out of Redwood’s seller payout (or negotiate a higher buyer-facing SKU to cover fees).
- Billing mapping: if you publish a per-1M-token SKU, usage records reported via the marketplace will be aggregated and billed to the buyer at the SKU unit price; Redwood will then receive payout minus marketplace fees. For subscription+usage-tier models, consider tier breakpoints aligned to the token volumes you provided (600M, 1.8B, 5B) to simplify procurement approval.

Next steps: we can help create the private-offer draft once Redwood confirms the buyer account ID, desired SKU structure (per-1M tokens vs subscription + tiers), and the buyer-facing unit price you want on the PO. If helpful, we also provide a sample private-offer template and a DocuSign flow for acceptance.

Sample support doc: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/help/private-offers (public)
DocuSign PO link (sample): https://docusign.com/samples/PO-Redwood-BrightCart

Best,
